# 300.00 USD of travel charged to a US dollar card at 1.35, then 500.00 USD
# paid onto the card from C — more than it owes.
#
# The card goes from owing 300.00 to holding a credit of 200.00. So 300.00 of
# the payment repays what the card owes, drawing down the card's owed cost
# basis at 1.35 and C's held one at 1.30, and the other 200.00 moves within
# the held side, from C to the card's credit, drawing down no cost basis and
# opening none. C's cost basis falls by the 300.00 the held side lost, not by
# the 500.00 C paid.
#
# Each split is valued at what it cost: C's 500.00 at 1.30, 650.00, and the
# card's 300.00 repaid at 1.35, 405.00, plus the 200.00 moved at the 1.30 it
# came at, 260.00. `$residual$` takes the 15.00 realized on repaying at 1.35 a
# debt with dollars that cost 1.30.
#
# Imported into the book usd_moved_out_of_an_empty_account.txt makes.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_a_balance_past_zero_has_a_cost_basis_on_the_other_side.py.
2034-01-20 * "Travel charged to the card"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Expenses:Travel 405.00 CAD
	Liabilities:USD Card -300.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "27/20"
		value: "-405.00"
		guid: "0a0a0000000000000000000000000008"

2034-02-01 * "Pay 500.00 USD onto the card from C"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:USD C -500.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "13/10"
		value: "-650.00"
		cost_basis_split_guid: "0a0a0000000000000000000000000003"
	Liabilities:USD Card 500.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "133/100"
		value: "665.00"
		cost_basis_split_guid: "0a0a0000000000000000000000000008"
	Income:FX Gain $residual$ CAD
